$comment: Tests that already fail (or flake) on main, measured at c36329b on 2026-10-20.
The CI test job fails on any failing test NOT in this list. Fixing one of
these is a separate PR; when you do, delete its entry. CI tells you when an
entry has stopped failing so the list cannot rot into a permanent excuse.
Never add an entry to make your own PR green — that is what the gate is for.

known.name: spec.md template validation > NFR:cost.tokens: Token optimization > should be reasonably concise overall
known.why: The spec.md template exceeds the token budget the test asserts. Pre-existing.

known.name: spec.md template validation > NFR:cost.instructions: Clear and actionable instructions > should have instruction blocks that are concise
known.why: Instruction-length assertion against the spec.md template. Pre-existing.

known.name: Annotation enforcement > Test coverage completeness > should have test @req for every active P1-P3 leaf requirement
known.why: 8 P1-P3 leaf requirements in .xe/features/feature-context/spec.md have no test @req annotation. PR #150 is addressing this.

known.name: FileReadAction > execute > should handle permission errors
known.why: Passes on macOS, fails on Linux CI, which is why it went unnoticed until this workflow existed. The test reads /root/protected-file.txt and allows only ['FileNotFound', 'FileReadFailed']. On macOS /root does not exist, so it gets FileNotFound. On a Linux runner /root exists and is unreadable by the runner user, so the action correctly returns FilePermissionDenied — a code the test forgot to allow. The production code is right; the expected list is incomplete. One-line fix, deliberately left out of the CI PR.

known.name: Playbook Engine Integration > end-to-end workflows > should enforce resource locking
known.why: FLAKY, not a hard failure. Passes in isolation (3/3) and fails under full-suite parallel load: playbook 1 releases the lock before playbook 2 tries to take it, so result2.status is 'completed' instead of 'failed'. A real race in the test, not the engine.
